title: Harmonize Resilience Policies: Cross-service Retry Semantics with Idempotency & Hedging
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Inconsistent retry/timeouts/backoff behavior across services and SDKs is causing SLO thrash, noisy failovers between regions, and customer-facing duplicate operations. Some services rely on client-side retries with weak idempotency contracts; others use server-side hedging with incompatible circuit-breaker interactions. Goal: define a single, backward-compatible resilience policy and SDK contract that harmonizes retries, timeouts, backoff strategies, idempotency key semantics, and hedged-request defaults. The policy must explicitly prescribe how multi-region failover, circuit breakers, and load-shedding interact so applications see predictable latency, cost, and correctness trade-offs.
acceptance_criteria: Normative spec published and reviewed by Runtime, SDK, and Platform teams (Confluence link in references)
SDKs (JS, Python, Go) implement new default resilience behavior behind a minor-version flag and include migration guides
Service proxies and runtime are updated to honor idempotency metadata and to avoid duplicative execution when client retries are used
Automated tests covering: single-region transient failures, cross-region failover, hedged requests vs client hedging, and circuit-breaker-triggered load-shedding
Observability: latency/error SLO dashboards for pre/post rollout, with alerting thresholds defined
Rollout plan validated on Canary traffic (10% production) with rollback criteria and mitigation playbooks
technical_notes: Core decisions: 1) Default client retry window: use 'SLO-aware deadline' = min(client-configured deadline, service-advertised SLO-window). 2) Default strategy: single conservative retry with exponential backoff base=250ms, max_backoff=2s, attempts=1 additional attempt; hedged requests opt-in via explicit header x-rw-hedge:level with levels {none, soft, aggressive}. 3) Idempotency: services must accept idempotency-key header (x-rw-idempotency-key) and guarantee exactly-once semantics for retried idempotent operations within 24h dedupe window by default. 4) Hedging semantics: when hedging is enabled at client or router, only operations flagged as 'idempotent' by service schema can be hedged unless service exposes 'hedge-safe=false'. 5) Circuit breakers: break on error-rate and latency percentiles tied to SLOs (p99 latency crossing 2x SLO for 2m) and surface breaker state via headers to clients to enable adaptive client backoff. 6) Load-shedding: runtime returns 429 with retry-after when queue depth > threshold; clients should respect retry-after and not immediate retry. 7) Multi-region failover: use 'sticky primary, async fallback' by default—client retries route to same region for fast recovery; when region mark unhealthy, subsequent requests route to fallback region with adjusted deadline (additional cross-region latency budget).
api_changes: Introduce x-rw-idempotency-key header (string) across RPCs and REST endpoints
Introduce x-rw-hedge header to opt-in hedged requests and define levels
Expose service capability metadata endpoint (/v1/capabilities) indicating hedge-safe and idempotency support
Clients expose 'observed-breaker-state' metric via telemetry to correlate retries with circuit breaker events
migration_steps: Step 1: Publish spec and capability endpoint contract; update internal confluence and notify teams
Step 2: Implement lightweight server-side idempotency middleware in 3 pilot services (billing, job-runner, inference-router)
Step 3: Release SDK flag `resilience_v2=true` in JS/Python/Go with docs and examples
Step 4: Monitor pilot services for duplicate-operation rate, latency SLO, and error budgets for 2 weeks
Step 5: Gradual rollout across services using canaries and region-aware traffic splits; enable hedging opt-in for controlled workloads
Step 6: Deprecate legacy client-only retry heuristics after 3 months with migration assistance
rollout_plan: Phase A (Canary): Enable on 3 pilot services in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 with 5% traffic for 7 days
Phase B (Incremental): Expand to platform-critical services (routing, auth) with 25% traffic for 14 days
Phase C (Full): Gradual account-level opt-in for SDK users, default flip after 90 days if no regressions
Rollback criteria: 1) p99 increase > 15% and error-rate increase > 1.5x for 10 minutes OR 2) duplicate-operation detections > 0.05% of requests over 1h
Mitigation playbooks: disable hedging globally, revert SDK flag, or increase dedupe window heuristics
observability_and_slo: Metrics to add: client.attempts.count, server.dedupe.hits, hedge.invocations, hedge.tail-reduction, breaker.state transitions, regional.failover.count, load_shed.rate. Dashboards: per-service SLO view showing pre/post rollout p50/p95/p99 and error budget burn. Alerts: automated pager when p99 latency > SLO*1.5 for 5m or when dedupe hits spike indicating retries causing duplicate side effects.
test_plan: Unit tests for idempotency middleware and dedupe store semantics (time-window edge cases)
Integration tests simulating network partitions to verify hedged vs sequential retry outcomes
Chaos testing: short-term region outage and verify client/route failover policies and circuit-breaker behavior
Load tests to validate load-shedding thresholds produce 429s and observe client respect of retry-after
SDK compatibility tests ensuring old clients still function (no hedging) when server advertises capability
